source.organization: City and County of Honolulu Department of Environmental Services
source.title: Rules and Guidelines for Residents
source.date_basis: The official City WordPress metadata for this page reports a modified timestamp of 2025-04-22.

evidence.locator: Rules and Guidelines for Residents > Regular Refuse
evidence.summary: The regular-refuse section explicitly includes mattresses and directs regular refuse to a refuse roll-off container or transfer-station pit floor; it asks residents to place refuse in bags when possible.
evidence.claim_scope: Mattresses delivered by Oʻahu residential households under the City's resident waste-drop-off rules.

records.supported_action: Take the mattress to an applicable City resident waste-drop-off facility and follow the attendant's direction to the regular-refuse roll-off container or transfer-station pit floor; bag it when possible.
important_restrictions: The page is for residents; commercial and government agency loads are not accepted.
Facility acceptance varies, and residents must follow posted signs and attendant directions.
General limits include no more than two loads per day and additional vehicle or large-load restrictions.

destination_or_program.name: City resident waste-drop-off system
destination_or_program.details: Regular-refuse roll-off container or transfer-station pit floor at an applicable City facility; this record does not select an individual site.

known_gaps: The inspected section does not establish mattress eligibility for curbside bulky pickup.
The source does not map mattress acceptance to individual sites or current hours.
records.verification_notes: The category-specific action and general drop-off qualifications were manually checked on the live official page. The claim is deliberately limited to drop-off.
records.duplicate_source_url_justification: The same official resident drop-off page contains separate, explicitly headed evidence for mattresses, propane containers, and battery types; each record uses its own locator and bounded claim.

source.organization: City and County of Honolulu Department of Environmental Services

evidence.locator: Rules and Guidelines for Residents > Compressed Gas
evidence.summary: The compressed-gas section covers empty, partially full, or full containers and lists propane tanks in the source-stated 5- and 20-gallon sizes and propane cylinders in the source-stated 16-ounce size.
evidence.claim_scope: Only the listed household propane container sizes delivered under the City's Oʻahu resident waste-drop-off rules.

records.supported_action: Take a source-listed household propane tank or cylinder to an applicable City resident waste-drop-off facility and follow posted signs and attendant directions.
important_restrictions: Supported tank sizes are limited to the source-stated 5 and 20 gallons; supported cylinders are limited to the source-stated 16 ounces.
Commercial-grade compressed gas, other industrial tanks, oxygen cylinders, and SCUBA tanks are prohibited.
Facility acceptance varies and the resident, vehicle, and daily-load rules apply.

destination_or_program.name: City resident waste-drop-off system
destination_or_program.details: An applicable City facility under the resident drop-off rules; this record does not select an individual site.

known_gaps: The source does not map each accepted propane size to a specific facility.
The inspected section provides no condition, valve, or transport-preparation instruction beyond distinguishing empty, partially full, and full containers.
records.verification_notes: The size wording is preserved as the City page states it and is not converted between gallons, pounds, or ounces.
records.duplicate_source_url_justification: The same official resident drop-off page contains separate, explicitly headed evidence for mattresses, propane containers, and battery types; each record uses its own locator and bounded claim.

source.organization: City and County of Honolulu Department of Environmental Services
source.title: E-waste Recycling at City Disposal Sites
source.date_basis: No publication, update, or claim-specific effective date was displayed on the inspected page.

evidence.locator: E-waste Recycling at City Disposal Sites > Material / Disposal Method > Acceptable items
evidence.summary: ENV states that e-waste bins are installed at its convenience centers and transfer stations and lists accepted devices including qualifying televisions, computers, monitors, printers, and other specifically named electronics; collected items will be recycled.
evidence.claim_scope: Only devices explicitly included in the City's accepted-items list for e-waste bins at City disposal sites.

evidence.locator: E-waste Recycling at City Disposal Sites > Unacceptable Items
evidence.summary: The same page excludes electronics integrated into motor vehicles, industrial/commercial/medical equipment, listed household appliances, telephones, and GPS units, but its telephone exclusion conflicts with VOIP telephones on the accepted list.
evidence.claim_scope: Exclusion and internal-conflict boundary for the broad televisions/electronics candidate.

records.supported_action: Take an electronic device that is explicitly on the City's accepted list to an e-waste bin at a listed City transfer station or convenience center for recycling.
important_restrictions: A television must meet the page's accepted television description, including a viewable screen of 9 inches or larger.
Devices integrated into motor vehicles or into the listed industrial, commercial, medical, or household equipment are not accepted.
No phone-specific action is supported because the source contradicts itself about VOIP telephones and telephones generally.

destination_or_program.name: City e-waste bins at disposal sites
destination_or_program.details: The page lists Kapaʻa, Kawailoa, and Keʻehi transfer stations and ʻEwa, Kapolei, Lāʻie, Wahiawā, Waiʻanae, Waimānalo, and Waipahu convenience centers.

known_gaps: The broad electronics candidate needs device-level category boundaries before production use.
Hours, temporary closures, and condition or quantity limits are not established by this record.
known_conflicts: The page lists VOIP telephones as acceptable but later lists a telephone of any type, including a mobile telephone, as unacceptable.
records.verification_notes: The accepted and unacceptable lists and every named City destination were manually checked. The conflicting phone guidance is excluded from the supported action.

evidence.locator: Rules and Guidelines for Residents > Battery
evidence.summary: The battery section directs alkaline and other single-use batteries to regular refuse; limits lead-acid acceptance to car and motorcycle batteries; and lists standalone lithium, lithium-ion, nickel-metal-hydride, and nickel-cadmium rechargeable batteries with taped terminals in a clear plastic bag.
evidence.claim_scope: Only the battery types, preparation, and Oʻahu resident disposal paths explicitly named by the City page.

records.supported_action: Put alkaline and other single-use household batteries in regular refuse. For a listed standalone rechargeable battery, tape the terminals, place it in a clear plastic bag, and take it to an applicable City resident waste-drop-off facility. Only car and motorcycle lead-acid batteries are supported by this record.
important_restrictions: Rechargeable drop-off guidance is limited to standalone lithium, lithium-ion, nickel-metal-hydride, and nickel-cadmium batteries.
Lead-acid acceptance is limited to car and motorcycle batteries.
Electric-vehicle batteries are prohibited under the resident drop-off rules.

destination_or_program.name: Regular refuse or City resident waste-drop-off system, depending on battery type
destination_or_program.details: Alkaline and other single-use batteries go in regular refuse; the source-listed standalone rechargeables and qualifying lead-acid batteries use applicable City resident drop-off facilities.

known_gaps: The source does not give a disposal action for damaged, swollen, leaking, or unidentified batteries.
Embedded batteries are outside this record's supported action.
records.verification_notes: The record preserves separate paths by battery type and does not treat the broad candidate label as one universal instruction.
records.duplicate_source_url_justification: The same official resident drop-off page contains separate, explicitly headed evidence for mattresses, propane containers, and battery types; each record uses its own locator and bounded claim.

source.organization: City and County of Honolulu Department of Environmental Services
source.title: Household Hazardous Waste (HHW)
source.date_basis: The page displays current event dates but no publication, update, or stable claim-specific effective date.

evidence.locator: Household Hazardous Waste > Disposal of HHW > Absorb and Put In Trash Can
evidence.summary: For small residential quantities, the table includes paint and primer in the absorb-and-trash route: liquid can be absorbed in a bag, sealed, and put in the trash, and paint can be air-dried in its can before trash disposal.
evidence.claim_scope: Small quantities of residential paint or primer covered by the page's absorb-and-trash row.

evidence.locator: Household Hazardous Waste > Disposal of HHW > Schedule an Appointment to Drop-Off
evidence.summary: The appointment list separately includes aluminum paint, lead paint, paint stripper, and paint thinner; the page says large quantities of any household hazardous waste require calling the City for instructions.
evidence.claim_scope: Named hazardous paint-related materials and large-quantity escalation that must not be collapsed into the ordinary small-quantity action.

records.supported_action: For a small residential quantity of paint or primer covered by the City's absorb-and-trash route, absorb the liquid in a plastic bag with absorbent material, seal the bag, and put it in the trash, or air-dry paint in the can before putting it in the trash. Use the City's HHW appointment process for the separately named hazardous paint-related materials.
important_restrictions: Large quantities of any household hazardous waste require calling the City's Refuse Division for disposal instructions.
Aluminum paint, lead paint, paint stripper, and paint thinner are listed for appointment-only HHW drop-off.
Event dates, registration status, deadlines, capacity, and appointment details are time-sensitive and must be rechecked on the live page.

destination_or_program.name: Household trash after source-specified preparation, or City HHW appointment for separately named materials
destination_or_program.details: The small-quantity paint/primer route ends in household trash after absorption or air drying; listed hazardous paint-related materials use a scheduled City HHW event.

known_gaps: The broad paint candidate requires type and quantity clarification before it can become a production category.
The page's event schedule is dynamic and cannot be treated as durable inventory data.
The record does not establish instructions for an unlabeled or otherwise unidentified coating.
records.verification_notes: The ordinary small-quantity route is kept separate from the named appointment-only materials and large-quantity escalation; no event date is encoded as a standing instruction.
